A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAS research and contain readable main text and Appendices A–H. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable assessment of the equations, figures, tables and supplementary material.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic sampling experiments and image-generation evaluations, including single-reward, multi-reward and online optimization results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports higher-compute Best-of-N results in Figure 8.

M1.justification: The tempered SMC procedure, Gaussian proposal, resampling and online-surrogate adaptations remain unchanged. Appendix C.1 newly discusses nested importance sampling as an alternative without incorporating it into DAS.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Gaussian-mixture and Swiss-roll experiments, image-generation evaluations using ImageNet/HPDv2 prompts, and the same reward objectives. Figure 8's extension uses the existing task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged, including Best-of-N and SMC in Appendix E. The newly cited Li et al. (2024) and nested importance sampling are discussed but do not become evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Figure 8 extends the reported Best-of-N compute sweep from approximately 3×10^4 to 10^5 TFLOPs. Appendix E still lists particle counts of 1–128, leaving the added points' particle counts unexplained. Other reported settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E's test-time-scaling analysis gains Best-of-N observations at two higher compute budgets, extending the existing sample-efficiency comparison. Tempering ablations, diffusion-sampler analyses and other case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 2's error bars are unchanged, and Figure 8 continues to show curves without uncertainty bars. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or statistical-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Figure 8 adds two Best-of-N points in each panel, with the final points approximately 0.2344 PickScore and 0.2955 HPSv2. Previously plotted values and DAS's lead are retained. Other figures and Tables 1–4 report unchanged results.

T1.justification: The propositions, assumptions, definitions, derivations and proofs remain unchanged. Appendix C.1 adds explanatory prose about sampling alternatives before the existing proof, without new mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free alignment, diversity, cross-reward generalization, tempering and applicability to single-reward, multi-reward and online optimization.

C2.justification: Appendix C.1 adds a rationale contrasting nested importance sampling's additional samples with the Gaussian approximation used for differentiable rewards. This expands the explanation of proposal choice; existing result interpretations and applicability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, pseudocode, reward processing and code-access statements remain unchanged. No additional configuration information accompanies Figure 8's new high-compute points.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 removes the restriction of previous SMC applications to inverse problems and class-conditional sampling, acknowledging guidance-free approaches through Li et al. (2024). Appendix C.1 adds connections to nested importance sampling, citing Li et al. and the newly added Naesseth et al. (2019).

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized rewriting in Section 2.2, an introductory paragraph in Appendix C.1, publication-header updates and punctuation edits. The overall organization and main narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 8 is redrawn with extended Best-of-N curves and slightly adjusted horizontal scaling. Publication headers, reference pagination and Appendix C.1 spacing change; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The higher-compute Best-of-N points make Figure 8's efficiency comparison more complete, while Sections 2.2 and C.1 improve acknowledgment of prior approaches and explain the proposal choice. These are limited gains. Appendix E's unchanged particle-count description leaves the added plot points incompletely documented.
